introduced_by_the_repairs.severity: MATERIAL - a functional regression reachable through the ordinary CLI, introduced by the D3 repair
introduced_by_the_repairs.title: The D3 glob matches other leases' records. A distinct lease whose slug is a '-'-boundary suffix of another's is falsely refused, permanently, with a message that names the wrong lease's receipt.
introduced_by_the_repairs.mechanism: write() globs `*-{slug}.json`. The leading `*` is meant to absorb the date, but it absorbs any prefix, so the pattern matches any record whose stem ENDS with the slug at a hyphen boundary - including another lease's record. _slug('lease:concern-a') = 'lease-concern-a'; _slug('lease:concern-b/lease/concern/a') = 'lease-concern-b-lease-concern-a'; fnmatch('2026-09-09-lease-concern-b-lease-concern-a.json', '*-lease-concern-a.json') is True.
introduced_by_the_repairs.reachability: Reachable through the ordinary CLI with ordinary concern names and no --lease-id override. Observed live in a clone at 70f154c: `take concern:b/lease/concern/a` then `take concern:a`, both exit 0. Closing lease:concern-b-lease-concern-a: REAL_EXIT=0, 'settlement recorded at reports/settlements/2026-09-09-lease-concern-b-lease-concern-a.json'. Then closing the entirely distinct lease:concern-a: REAL_EXIT=1, 'REFUSED SETTLEMENT_ALREADY_RECORDED: reports/settlements/2026-09-09-lease-concern-b-lease-concern-a.json already records a different settlement for lease:concern-a (receipt receipt:long, this close carries receipt:short).'
introduced_by_the_repairs.consequences: Three, and the second is the serious one. (a) A legitimate closure is refused and the lease is left HELD with nothing recorded; `status` confirmed lease:concern-a still HELD. The refusal is deterministic, so that lease can never be closed while the other record exists. (b) The refusal message is FALSE: it asserts that the named file 'already records a different settlement for lease:concern-a', and that file records a settlement for a different lease entirely. A participant reading that refusal is told a record exists for a lease that has none. (c) Because `existing[0]` takes the lexicographically first match, the change's own idempotency claim breaks: with lease:concern-b-lease-concern-a recorded on 2026-09-09 and lease:concern-a correctly recorded on 2026-09-10, re-running the IDENTICAL close of lease:concern-a is REFUSED, even though its own matching record is on disk. Observed directly: 'SettlementRefused: ...2026-09-09-lease-concern-b-lease-concern-a.json already records a different settlement for lease:concern-a (receipt receipt:B, this close carries receipt:A)'. The docstring on write() and test_re_running_the_same_closure_is_idempotent both state the opposite.
introduced_by_the_repairs.relation_to_the_prior_reading: The prior reading recorded D7, _slug non-injectivity, as MINOR and explicitly 'latent, not reachable through the CLI'. The D3 repair converts that latent hazard into a reachable one and widens it: the glob does not require two slugs to be equal, only that one be a hyphen-boundary suffix of the other, which is a far larger collision class. Anchoring the pattern to the date - for example `[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-{slug}.json` - would close it, and reading lease_id out of each candidate record rather than trusting the filename would close it properly.
introduced_by_the_repairs.not_a_finding: Cost is not a concern. write() with 5000 sibling records measured 4.6 ms.

verdict: DISSENT, narrowed. Three of the four named defects are closed in behaviour and one is closed properly. D1 is closed: the control at b7c85c0 reproduces the silent no-record close from a subdirectory and the subject writes the record under the repository root, while still refusing outside a tree. D2 is closed and is the only repair whose case can fail - it is behavioural, it reaches the record path rather than being short-circuited by the lease evaluator, and my M1 mutation fails it. D3 is closed: the cross-midnight sequence produced two contradicting records at b7c85c0 and is refused at 70f154c with both receipts named. D9 is closed for its message: the absolute path is gone and cannot structurally return through that string. The dissent is not that a named defect stayed open. It is that the D3 repair introduced NEW-1, a CLI-reachable regression that permanently refuses a legitimate distinct lease, tells the operator something false about which lease has a record, and breaks the idempotency the change itself claims; and that three of the four repairs (D1, D3, D9) carry no case that can see the defect they repaired, with D1's guard demonstrably defeasible under a mutation that leaves the test module, lint.py and verify.py all exit 0.

what_would_defeat_this_finding: NEW-1: a demonstration that no two lease ids reachable through sov_lease.py can stand in the hyphen-boundary suffix relation - for example a validator on --lease-id and on derived ids that refuses it. I reached it with two ordinary `take` invocations and no override, so such a validator does not exist today. Alternatively, a ruling that a false refusal is the safe direction and an operator is expected to read the named path; that would answer (a) and (b) but not (c), the broken idempotency, where the lease's own correct record is on disk and the close is still refused.

NEW-2: a case anywhere in the repository that executes cmd_close with CWD outside the repository root and asserts a record appears under the root. I ran the full suite, lint.py and verify.py against the equal-line-count M3 mutation and all three were green, so if such a case exists it is not reached by any of those three commands. Also defeating: a ruling that a source-text guard is sufficient for this class, which would contradict the reasoning the builder gave for the D2 repair in that same commit.

NEW-3: a case that writes a settlement on one date and re-writes the same lease on another and asserts the refusal, or any case asserting the SETTLEMENT_UNWRITABLE text excludes an absolute path. Reverting each repair left the suite green, so neither exists in scripts/tests/test_lease_settlement.py; I did not exhaustively read every test module in the tree, and a case living elsewhere would collapse this item.

D1/D3/D9 'closed' verdicts: evidence that my clone-based harness differs materially from the shared-worktree environment. The clones share no .git/sov-sessions with the primary tree, which is what made this safe under trap T6, but it also means every lease id used here was fresh. I do not believe this affects any verdict, and I record it because it is the assumption the method rests on.

The whole reading: evidence that the tree moved underneath it. It did not. The primary checkout read 0053654 with an empty status before and after, the subject resolved to 70f154c with tree 5a7d7d8 at both ends, verify.py was run twice with the same verdict, and the shared lease store's mtime predates the first probe.
